jobs.title: Vice President, Technology Operations
jobs.description:
About the Role

The organization is seeking an experienced technology operations leader with direct experience in data, data operations, hosting infrastructure, public and private cloud environments, development operations, and cybersecurity. This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the adoption and usage of advanced AI technologies across the operations organization to improve internal efficiency and accelerate product and business outcomes.
Track technology operational trends and AI advancements, identifying creative solutions to drive efficiency and greater throughput.
Provide leadership, vision, and strategy driving automation, stability, and availability of technology infrastructure leveraging cloud and on-premise technologies to support business agility.
Drive innovation across security, data privacy, data operations, development operations, and infrastructure.
Define the technology operations strategy and roadmap to support current and future business needs for scalability, capacity, and quality of service, including performance, reliability, and business continuity.
Define requirements for new technology implementations and communicate them to key business stakeholders.
Partner with senior leadership across the business to realize measurable outcomes aligned with business expectations.
Drive the execution of security, data, infrastructure, and technology operations initiatives to achieve targets for scalability, performance, and availability.
Assess and communicate risks associated with technology-related investments and purchases.
Support business growth initiatives by aligning technology operations with business strategy.
Develop business case justifications and cost-benefit analyses for technology operations spending and initiatives.
Implement the people, processes, and technologies necessary to meet customer demands.
Define, maintain, and present regular operational metrics to executive leadership, including overall security, data, and infrastructure health, risk areas, and productivity.
Define, measure, and improve technology standards across the organization to establish a technology-enabled competitive edge.
Provide technical assessments and due diligence for potential acquisitions.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or higher in computer science, information systems, or engineering.
15 years of experience managing technology operations across development operations, data, infrastructure, and cybersecurity.
Extensive knowledge and direct experience applying AI tools and methodologies to improve operational efficiency.
Strong technical background in environments featuring a heterogeneous mix of on-premise, hosted, and cloud hardware and software.
Experience with operational technologies for the deployment, maintenance, and monitoring of large-scale SaaS platforms.
Experience with hosting operations and leading cloud migrations involving AWS, Azure, and GCP.
Experience managing vendor relationships and negotiating contracts to optimize expense costs.
Strong executive communication skills with the ability to convey technical details and strategy to non-technical leadership.
Demonstrated success leading modernization and transformation initiatives across data and infrastructure environments.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity methodologies and practices.
Demonstrated success leading large, diverse global teams and attracting and retaining talent.
Expert knowledge of technology environments, including networks, operating systems, databases, and application and web servers.
Technical experience in systems networking, databases, infrastructure, and user support.
Experience defining standardized operating procedures and services across operational disciplines.
Experience in strategic technology planning, execution, and policy development.
Experience with business processes, management, and budgeting.
Strong understanding of project management principles.
Proven experience in planning, organization, and development.
Demonstrated ability to apply technology solutions to business problems.
Experience with acquisition due diligence and integrations.

The salary range for Zone 1 (National Average) is $282,000 to $322,000 USD per year.

Compensation is determined by experience, qualifications, role requirements, and location based on a four-tier geographic zone model (Zone 1: National Average; Zone 2: Moderately Higher Cost Regions; Zone 3: High-Cost Regions; Zone 4: Lower-Cost Regions).
Eligible employees have the opportunity for variable pay.
Benefits include health coverage and an employee assistance program.

The hiring organization is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability status.

For California residents, applicant personal information is processed in accordance with the California Consumer Privacy Act, and specific geographic compensation details will be provided during initial screening.

jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Director of Information Technology
will oversee the internal technology estate end to end and lead the team responsible for running it. Reporting directly to the Chief Information Officer, this full-time role based in the United States covers identity, endpoints, networking, collaboration, service management, and the internal artificial intelligence platform across a distributed, remote-first organization.

This position is designed for a leader experienced in building and scaling internal technology through periods of rapid growth, possessing the capability to construct a multi-year roadmap while maintaining the ability to resolve operational issues directly. The role collaborates closely with Security, Engineering, Finance, and Human Resources leadership while managing vendor and managed service provider relationships.

Key Responsibilities

Build and execute a multi-year internal technology roadmap across identity, endpoints, networking, collaboration, and service management.
Tie technology investments directly to business outcomes with defined success measures.
Define internal delivery models versus services managed through partners and managed service providers.
Establish IT governance, operating standards, architecture reviews, and change management.
Design the internal IT function, build business cases for headcount, and hire and develop team members.
Mentor the team and establish clear ownership, on-call schedules, and escalation models.
Build and maintain the internal service catalog and associated service level agreements.
Own internal AI tool use case development, rollout, training, and adoption measurement.
Partner with the organization's AI practice so internal usage directly informs client-facing delivery.
Apply financial engineering to the internal AI estate by developing unit-cost models, forecasting consumption, negotiating commitments and reserved capacity, and holding AI expenditures accountable to measured productivity gains.
Own endpoint management, configuration baselines, patching, and hardware lifecycles using Intune or equivalent systems.
Manage the Microsoft 365 collaboration environment, including Teams, SharePoint, and Exchange governance.
Define and enforce device posture requirements for a remote-first workforce.
Direct internal network architecture, remote access, and secure connectivity models.
Manage the internal cloud and hosting footprint, including capacity, cost, and resilience.
Direct backup, recovery, and business continuity for internal systems with tested recovery objectives.
Establish and mature IT service management across intake, incident, problem, request, and change processes.
Publish operational metrics and systematically eliminate key sources of employee workflow friction.
Oversee the onboarding and offboarding technology experience in partnership with Human Resources.
Manage the internal IT budget, financial forecasts, and software licensing positions.
Rationalize the SaaS estate and direct renewals, contract negotiations, and vendor terms.
Hold external partners and managed service providers accountable to defined service levels.
Partner with security leadership to execute the IT components of the broader security program.
Support SOC 2 and ISO audit readiness, including control operation and evidence collection.
Own vulnerability management and remediation across internal systems and endpoints.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of information technology experience, including proven experience leading teams or owning a technology function.
Demonstrated experience building and scaling internal IT within a distributed or remote-first company during periods of rapid growth.
Experience presenting technology strategy, investment recommendations, operational risks, and performance metrics to executive leadership.
Deep hands-on experience with Microsoft 365, Entra ID, endpoint management (Intune or equivalent), and SaaS administration at scale.
Demonstrated ownership of internal AI adoption and governance, including policy creation, data handling, and change management.
Strong security fluency, with the ability to partner credibly with executive security leadership and translate technical risk into business terms.
Proven experience supporting SOC 2, ISO, or related regulated compliance and audit requirements.
Experience managing IT budgets and negotiating contracts with vendors and managed service providers.
Ability to communicate technical trade-offs clearly to both executive and technical audiences, in writing and in person.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience operating within a solutions provider, managed service provider (MSP), or technology consulting environment.
Relevant industry certifications, such as ITIL, Microsoft certifications, CISSP, CISM, PMP, or equivalent credentials.

Compensation and Benefits

Full-time employment status.
Discretionary incentive compensation and bonus opportunities based on individual and organizational performance.
Comprehensive health coverage, including medical, dental, and vision insurance.
401(k) retirement plan with an employer match.
Flexible time off, paid holidays, and paid sick leave.
Short-term and long-term disability insurance.
Life insurance.
Paid parental leave.

Employment Notices

The organization is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds. Qualified candidates are considered without regard to any legally protected status. This role is subject to applicable employment laws based on work location. In compliance with pay transparency laws, final compensation is determined based on experience, skills, and location. jobs.title: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery, VP - Technology Resilience and Enterprise Technology
jobs.description:
Blackstone is the world’s largest alternative asset manager. Blackstone seeks to deliver compelling returns for institutional and individual investors by strengthening the companies in which the firm invests. Blackstone’s over $1.3 trillion in assets under management include global investment strategies focused on real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, secondaries and hedge funds. Further information is available at www.blackstone.com. Follow @blackstone on LinkedIn, X (Twitter), and Instagram.

Business Description

Blackstone Technology & Innovations (BXTI) is the technology organization at the core of Blackstone’s businesses and growth initiatives. We design and deliver enterprise platforms and services that manage risk, create efficiency, and improve transparency across the firm and its global community of investors and portfolio companies.

BXTI operates with an entrepreneurial mindset—collaborative, fast‑moving, and outcome‑driven—while maintaining the rigor required to support a complex global enterprise. We value leadership, accountability, and continuous improvement, and we expect our leaders to help the firm maintain its competitive edge.

Job Description

Blackstone Technology & Innovations (BXTI) is seeking a highly experienced and strategic Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Leader to establish, drive, and continuously grow the firm’s technology resilience capabilities across infrastructure, applications, platforms, cloud services, and end-user technology.

This role is responsible for ensuring that technology services can withstand, respond to, and recover from operational disruptions, cyber incidents, infrastructure failures, third-party outages, and other business-impacting events. This role includes being accountable for the overarching frameworks, processes, recovery strategies, and governance structures, while working closely with each technology tower to ensure adherence to program.

Reporting into the firm’s Enterprise Technology function with a dotted line into the firm’s global Business Continuity Leader, this position owns technology recovery readiness across the technology estate and serves as the primary leader for technology continuity and disaster recovery governance. The successful candidate will build a culture of resilience, establish measurable recovery capabilities, drive accountability with service owners, and ensure that continuity planning evolves alongside the firm’s technology modernization efforts.

Key Responsibilities

Technology Resilience Strategy & Governance

Develop and maintain the technology resilience strategy, roadmap, standards, and operating model.
Establish governance frameworks, policies, and controls that align business continuity, disaster recovery, operational resilience, cyber recovery, and crisis management capabilities.
Define technology resilience metrics, key risk indicators, and executive reporting.
Ensure resilience requirements are embedded into architecture reviews, platform design decisions, cloud adoption initiatives, and technology transformation programs.
Drive continuous improvement based on testing outcomes, incidents, audits, and emerging threats.

Technology Recovery Planning

Ensure and track that every critical application, platform, infrastructure service, and technology team has documented, maintained, and approved recovery plans.
Establish standards for Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs), Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs), service criticality classifications, recovery dependencies, and minimum viable operating levels.
Support the maintenance and validation of a technology service inventory that maps applications, infrastructure, cloud services, vendors, and business dependencies.
Ensure all service owners understand their recovery obligations and remain accountable for plan quality and readiness.
Drive collaboration with Business Units, Corporate Functions, and individual offices to prepare for BCP events based on specific needs of impacted groups, teams, and locations.

Disaster Recovery Readiness

Lead the firm’s technology disaster recovery program across cloud infrastructure, on-premise platforms, core applications, network services, end-user technology, and collaboration platforms.
Work with the firm’s Chief Architect to validate that recovery architectures, failover capabilities, backup solutions, and resiliency patterns meet business requirements.
Partner with engineering and infrastructure teams to identify individual points of failure and remediation priorities.
Drive technology resilience requirements into platform lifecycle management and modernization efforts.
Support internal audits, risk assessments, client due diligence requests, and regulatory reviews related to resilience and recovery preparedness.
Establish reporting processes that provide visibility into preparedness, testing results, residual risks, and remediation progress.

Testing & Exercising

Develop and maintain a comprehensive testing program for all critical technology services.
Establish standards for tabletop exercises, simulation exercises, technical failover tests, cyber recovery exercises, and full-scale disaster recovery events.
Ensure each technology domain maintains documented test schedules, test plans, results, lessons learned, and remediation actions.
Facilitate executive and technology leadership participation in crisis simulations and recovery exercises.
Track remediation actions through completion and validate risk reduction outcomes.

Operational Resilience & Crisis Management

Serve as the technology point of contact during major incidents and crisis events.
Coordinate cross-functional technology recovery efforts during disruptive events.
Partner with Cyber Security, Infrastructure, Cloud, Operations, and Engineering teams during incidents and technology outages.
Support executive crisis management teams with impact assessment, recovery planning, and readiness reporting.
Provide clear executive-level communications regarding technology recovery status, risks, and dependencies.

Required Experience

10+ years of experience in technology risk, resilience, disaster recovery, infrastructure operations, technology governance, cybersecurity, or enterprise technology leadership.
Demonstrated experience leading large-scale BCP/DR or operational resilience programs within a complex enterprise environment.
Strong understanding of disaster recovery, business continuity management, operational resilience, cyber recovery, incident command structures, cloud recovery architectures, infrastructure resilience, and technology risk management.
Experience managing enterprise-wide testing and exercise programs.
Experience engaging with executive leadership, regulators, auditors, and risk functions.
Financial services or highly regulated industry experience preferred.
Demonstrated experience building strong partnerships across engineering, infrastructure, security, cloud, operations, and business teams.
Proven history of influencing without authority, establishing strong accountability among service owners for resilience readiness.

The duties and responsibilities described here are not exhaustive and additional assignments, duties, or responsibilities may be required of this position. Assignments, duties, and responsibilities may be changed at any time, with or without notice, by Blackstone in its sole discretion.

Expected annual base salary range:

$160,000 - $225,000

Actual base salary within that range will be determined by several components including but not limited to the individual's experience, skills, qualifications and job location. For roles located outside of the US, please disregard the posted salary bands as these roles will follow a separate compensation process based on local market comparables.

Additional compensation and benefits offered in connection with the role consist of comprehensive health benefits, including but not limited to medical, dental, vision, and FSA benefits; paid time off; life insurance; 401(k) plan; and discretionary bonuses. Certain employees may also be eligible for equity and other incentive compensation at Blackstone’s sole discretion.

Role Overview

As the Director of AgentExchange Security & Labs, you will serve as a strategic architect and operational lead for our global platform innovation program and driving ecosystem security. Strategic Guidance & Ecosystem Governance

Multi-Year Roadmap Advisory: Set and champion the 2–3 year strategic vision for the Labs portfolio, ensuring close alignment with core corporate initiatives and platform releases.

new_jobs.description:
Blackstone is the world’s largest alternative asset manager. Blackstone seeks to deliver compelling returns for institutional and individual investors by strengthening the companies in which the firm invests. Blackstone’s over $1.3 trillion in assets under management include global investment strategies focused on real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, secondaries and hedge funds. Further information is available at www.blackstone.com. Follow @blackstone on LinkedIn, X (Twitter), and Instagram.

Business Description

Blackstone Technology & Innovations (BXTI) is the technology organization at the core of Blackstone’s businesses and growth initiatives. We design and deliver enterprise platforms and services that manage risk, create efficiency, and improve transparency across the firm and its global community of investors and portfolio companies.

BXTI operates with an entrepreneurial mindset—collaborative, fast‑moving, and outcome‑driven—while maintaining the rigor required to support a complex global enterprise. We value leadership, accountability, and continuous improvement, and we expect our leaders to help the firm maintain its competitive edge.

Job Description

Blackstone Technology & Innovations (BXTI) is seeking a highly experienced and strategic Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Leader to establish, drive, and continuously grow the firm’s technology resilience capabilities across infrastructure, applications, platforms, cloud services, and end-user technology.

This role is responsible for ensuring that technology services can withstand, respond to, and recover from operational disruptions, cyber incidents, infrastructure failures, third-party outages, and other business-impacting events. This role includes being accountable for the overarching frameworks, processes, recovery strategies, and governance structures, while working closely with each technology tower to ensure adherence to program.

Reporting into the firm’s Enterprise Technology function with a dotted line into the firm’s global Business Continuity Leader, this position owns technology recovery readiness across the technology estate and serves as the primary leader for technology continuity and disaster recovery governance. The successful candidate will build a culture of resilience, establish measurable recovery capabilities, drive accountability with service owners, and ensure that continuity planning evolves alongside the firm’s technology modernization efforts.

Key Responsibilities

Technology Resilience Strategy & Governance

Develop and maintain the technology resilience strategy, roadmap, standards, and operating model.
Establish governance frameworks, policies, and controls that align business continuity, disaster recovery, operational resilience, cyber recovery, and crisis management capabilities.
Define technology resilience metrics, key risk indicators, and executive reporting.
Ensure resilience requirements are embedded into architecture reviews, platform design decisions, cloud adoption initiatives, and technology transformation programs.
Drive continuous improvement based on testing outcomes, incidents, audits, and emerging threats.

Technology Recovery Planning

Ensure and track that every critical application, platform, infrastructure service, and technology team has documented, maintained, and approved recovery plans.
Establish standards for Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs), Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs), service criticality classifications, recovery dependencies, and minimum viable operating levels.
Support the maintenance and validation of a technology service inventory that maps applications, infrastructure, cloud services, vendors, and business dependencies.
Ensure all service owners understand their recovery obligations and remain accountable for plan quality and readiness.
Drive collaboration with Business Units, Corporate Functions, and individual offices to prepare for BCP events based on specific needs of impacted groups, teams, and locations.

Disaster Recovery Readiness

Lead the firm’s technology disaster recovery program across cloud infrastructure, on-premise platforms, core applications, network services, end-user technology, and collaboration platforms.
Work with the firm’s Chief Architect to validate that recovery architectures, failover capabilities, backup solutions, and resiliency patterns meet business requirements.
Partner with engineering and infrastructure teams to identify individual points of failure and remediation priorities.
Drive technology resilience requirements into platform lifecycle management and modernization efforts.
Support internal audits, risk assessments, client due diligence requests, and regulatory reviews related to resilience and recovery preparedness.
Establish reporting processes that provide visibility into preparedness, testing results, residual risks, and remediation progress.

Testing & Exercising

Develop and maintain a comprehensive testing program for all critical technology services.
Establish standards for tabletop exercises, simulation exercises, technical failover tests, cyber recovery exercises, and full-scale disaster recovery events.
Ensure each technology domain maintains documented test schedules, test plans, results, lessons learned, and remediation actions.
Facilitate executive and technology leadership participation in crisis simulations and recovery exercises.
Track remediation actions through completion and validate risk reduction outcomes.

Operational Resilience & Crisis Management

Serve as the technology point of contact during major incidents and crisis events.
Coordinate cross-functional technology recovery efforts during disruptive events.
Partner with Cyber Security, Infrastructure, Cloud, Operations, and Engineering teams during incidents and technology outages.
Support executive crisis management teams with impact assessment, recovery planning, and readiness reporting.
Provide clear executive-level communications regarding technology recovery status, risks, and dependencies.

Required Experience

10+ years of experience in technology risk, resilience, disaster recovery, infrastructure operations, technology governance, cybersecurity, or enterprise technology leadership.
Demonstrated experience leading large-scale BCP/DR or operational resilience programs within a complex enterprise environment.
Strong understanding of disaster recovery, business continuity management, operational resilience, cyber recovery, incident command structures, cloud recovery architectures, infrastructure resilience, and technology risk management.
Experience managing enterprise-wide testing and exercise programs.
Experience engaging with executive leadership, regulators, auditors, and risk functions.
Financial services or highly regulated industry experience preferred.
Demonstrated experience building strong partnerships across engineering, infrastructure, security, cloud, operations, and business teams.
Proven history of influencing without authority, establishing strong accountability among service owners for resilience readiness.

The duties and responsibilities described here are not exhaustive and additional assignments, duties, or responsibilities may be required of this position. Assignments, duties, and responsibilities may be changed at any time, with or without notice, by Blackstone in its sole discretion.

Expected annual base salary range:

$160,000 - $225,000

Actual base salary within that range will be determined by several components including but not limited to the individual's experience, skills, qualifications and job location. For roles located outside of the US, please disregard the posted salary bands as these roles will follow a separate compensation process based on local market comparables.

Additional compensation and benefits offered in connection with the role consist of comprehensive health benefits, including but not limited to medical, dental, vision, and FSA benefits; paid time off; life insurance; 401(k) plan; and discretionary bonuses. Certain employees may also be eligible for equity and other incentive compensation at Blackstone’s sole discretion.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including but not limited to hiring, placement, promotion, termination, transfer, leave of absence, compensation, and training. Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Job Description

Role Overview

As the Director of AgentExchange Security & Labs, you will serve as a strategic architect and operational lead for our global platform innovation program and driving ecosystem security. This is a high-impact Individual Contributor (IC) role designed for a visionary operator who excels at driving cross-functional alignment without direct reporting authority.

You will be responsible for guiding matrixed teams to own the end-to-end lifecycle of Labs solutions and Security Review operational processes—from identifying critical market gaps to scaling adoption across the Trailblazer ecosystem. A core focus of this role is modernizing our ecosystem operating model by embedding AI-assisted workflows across roadmapping, data analysis, and security review processes, while acting as a critical business stakeholder for AgentExchange partner security.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Guidance & Ecosystem Governance

Multi-Year Roadmap Advisory: Set and champion the 2–3 year strategic vision for the Labs portfolio, ensuring close alignment with core corporate initiatives and platform releases.
Executive GM Partnership: Act as a strategic advisor to Cloud GMs and Product Management teams on Labs investment strategies, retirements, and how the portfolio drives ecosystem value.
Cross-Functional Influence: Build and maintain highly durable, collaborative partnerships across matrixed organizations, including Legal, Product Security, Marketing, Solution Engineering, and Trailblazer Community teams.

Security Review Program & Operations

Product Security Partnership: Act as the primary operational liaison to the Product Security team to co-design ecosystem security programs, review methodologies, and compliance frameworks.
Escalation Management: Serve as the designated lead for high-priority partner security escalations, unblocking technical reviews and resolving critical vulnerabilities with executive stakeholders.
Commercial Fee Architecture: Own the business and operational strategy for the Security Review fee structure, balancing ecosystem growth with program cost-recovery objectives.
Ecosystem Security Guardrails: Partner deeply with Product Managers and Product Security to optimize the technical baseline, significantly reducing the cycle time for complex ISV and Labs solutions to clear the AgentExchange Security Review.

AI-Accelerated Program Architecture

AI Tooling & Automation Strategy: Architect and own the AgentExchange Security & Labs AI-tooling roadmap to automate highly repetitive operational processes and scale ecosystem programs.
Advanced Content Automation: Lead the strategy for leveraging generative AI to build "Content-in-a-Box" deployment kits (including demo scripts, technical blog posts, and enablement decks), maintaining strict brand voice while shortening go-to-market timelines.

Data-Driven Insights & Reporting

Executive Narratives: Synthesize complex data regarding program health—such as install rates, user reviews, security posture, failure reasons, and platform adoption—into compelling, executive-level health reports for senior leadership.
Data Synthesis at Scale: Direct the harmonization of large, disparate datasets into clear, actionable, executive-ready "sources of truth" dashboards.
Strategic Lifecycle Actions: Translate ecosystem telemetry into definitive operational recommendations, such as sunsetting underperforming solutions or doubling down on trending technical categories.

Ecosystem Engagement & Thought Leadership

Public Representation: Present as a trusted platform expert at major community events and conferences (e.g., Dreamforce, World Tours, Community Dreamin’ events), demonstrating the "Art of the Possible" using Labs solutions.
Demand Generation Strategy: Coordinate with Marketing teams to drive visibility, organic demand, and community engagement for high-impact Labs solutions via social channels and the Trailblazer network.

Required Experience & Qualifications

10+ Years of Leadership: Extensive experience in program management, technical product management, or GTM strategy within a high-growth SaaS enterprise.
Proven Influence Without Authority: Documented success leading massive, cross-functional matrixed initiatives and aligning executive stakeholders up to the SVP/EVP level without direct reports.
Security Program Experience: Strong background navigating complex software security reviews, managing high-stakes client/partner escalations, or designing program operational structures.
AI & Automation Fluency: Practical, hands-on experience embedding LLM/AI workflows into business operational workflows to compress cycle times or scale organizational output, backed by measurable lift metrics.
Salesforce Ecosystem Expertise: Deep architectural and conceptual familiarity with the Salesforce platform (Admin, Developer, and Architect personas), AgentExchange, and the Trailblazer ecosystem.
Preferred Certifications: Salesforce Certified Administrator, Platform Developer I, and Platform Developer II.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

new_jobs.title: Senior Manager, Digital & IT Strategy
new_jobs.description:
About Chartis

The challenges facing US healthcare are longstanding and all too familiar. We are Chartis, and we believe in better. We work with more than 1,900 organizations annually to develop and activate transformative strategies, operating models, and organizational enterprises that make US healthcare more affordable, accessible, safe, and human. With more than 1,450 professionals, we help providers, payers, technology innovators, retail companies, and investors create and embrace solutions that tangibly and materially reshape healthcare for the better. Our family of brands—Chartis, Jarrard, Greeley, and HealthScape Advisors—is 100% focused on healthcare, and each has a longstanding commitment to helping transform healthcare in big and small ways. Believe in better.

Chartis has offices in Boston, Chicago, New York, Washington D.C., and Nashville.

This is a remote role with flexibility to live anywhere in the United States. Proximity to a Chartis office is preferred but not required. Client travel varies based on project needs, client preferences, and key milestones.

Role Overview

Senior Managers in our Digital & Technology Transformation line of business are integral members of our consulting teams, leading junior colleagues on projects with healthcare provider clients typically spanning 3-6 months in duration. Our projects are focused in the following areas: IT operational performance improvement, digital & IT governance & program management, M&A/PE IT diligence & integration, PMO optimization, enterprise digital strategy, and digital business case development.

Responsibilities

Manage the overall project, balancing work effort and input from clients and colleagues to achieve goals
Act as a trusted advisor to clients, drawing upon healthcare knowledge and insights
Coach and mentor junior staff, driving the development of their skills and knowledge
Produce sophisticated, compelling deliverables that motivate clients to action
Support the firm’s growth through contributions to internal initiatives

Qualifications And Desired Skills

Minimum of 5 years of direct experience working with healthcare providers on strategic initiatives, preferably in a consulting / professional services environment
Experience working with healthcare provider digital and IT environments, including familiarity with major clinical, enterprise, and digital platforms (e.g., Epic, Oracle Health/Cerner, MEDITECH, etc.), and the ability to think strategically about how technology enables provider strategy, operations, performance, and transformation
Familiarity with AI technologies and their implications for healthcare providers, with the ability to use AI-enabled tools effectively while applying independent critical thinking and professional judgment
Advanced degree preferred (e.g., MBA, MHA, MPH), or equivalent experience developing business cases, financial models, and strategic recommendations.
Excellent critical thinking and analytical skills
Outstanding verbal and written communication skills
Proficient in Microsoft Office; experience with Tableau is a plus

Salary range: $160,000-$200,000 plus may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus. The salary range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills, experience, training, licensure and certifications, practice area, and other business and organizational needs. In addition, Chartis offers several benefits including medical, dental, vision, HSA, FSA, disability insurance, life insurance, 401(k) match, paid time off, wellness stipend, and additional voluntary benefits.

At Chartis, we pride ourselves on having a diverse workforce. We value and celebrate the uniqueness of individuals and the different perspectives they provide. We offer equal opportunity employment regardless of race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability status, age, marital status, or protected veteran status.
